title: Appeal TE Sang Soo Ryoo vs. Korean Capital Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC answered the issue “No”: the judicial commission did not follow BCO 32 and 34. It sustained the appeal and remanded the case to Presbytery for a new trial in compliance with those provisions. It expressly declined to pass on the adequacy of the citations or to comment on the merits. The source does not state whether the prior finding or three-year suspension was vacated.
first_summary: The SJC sustained an assistant pastor’s appeal from a three-year suspension from the sacraments after a Korean Capital Presbytery commission found him guilty of participating in an unconstitutional presbytery meeting. The commission failed BCO 32 and 34 because no indictment was served, no prosecutor was clearly appointed, and no trial minutes appeared in the record; service of an indictment with a witness list was critical. The case was remanded for a new trial; the SJC did not address the merits or citation adequacy.
summary: The SJC sustained an assistant pastor’s appeal from a three-year suspension from the sacraments after a Korean Capital Presbytery commission found him guilty of participating in the call of an allegedly unconstitutional presbytery meeting. The decisive defect was procedural: no indictment was served, no prosecutor was clearly appointed, and no trial minutes appeared in the record; service of an indictment with a witness list was critical. The case was remanded for a new trial, and the SJC expressly did not reach the merits or citation adequacy.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Header lines 1–5 identify the SJC, 30th General Assembly (2002), and disposition “sustained.” Lines 86–90 show the panel adopted the statement, issue, judgment, and reasoning, with 17 concurrences, 0 dissents, 1 recusal, 2 disqualifications, and 4 absences.
evidence_notes.dispute: Lines 18–48 state that TE Sang Soo Ryoo, an assistant pastor, was charged for participating in the call of an “unconstitutional” meeting of Korean Capital Presbytery; a commission found him guilty and imposed a three-year suspension from the sacraments, which Presbytery approved. Lines 54 and 58 frame the issue as whether the Judicial Commission followed BCO procedures.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Lines 56–84 contain the judgment and reasoning: the commission did not follow BCO 32 and 34; no indictment was ever served, it was unclear whether one was prepared or a prosecutor formally appointed, and the record lacked trial minutes. Because proper service of an indictment with a witness list was critical and did not happen, the case was remanded for a new trial.
evidence_notes.qualifications: Lines 80–84 expressly say the SJC was not passing on the adequacy of the citations and was not commenting on the merits. Lines 40–46 show the commission/Presbytery action but do not state whether the suspension was vacated or what occurred after remand.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: None. The SJC adjudicated the appeal through its own adopted panel statement, issue, judgment, and reasoning; no separate decision is incorporated by reference in the source.

source_limits: The source is the printed General Assembly report. It does not reproduce the underlying record, indictment, trial minutes, or post-remand proceedings, and it does not state whether the three-year suspension remained in effect after remand.
benchmark_examples: A01: distinguish conviction, censure, and administrative suspension; this source does not say whether the three-year suspension was vacated after the procedural remand.
A03: when separate issues have different outcomes, preserve each remedy; here the SJC resolved only the procedural issue and expressly declined the merits.
